description: Project: Dancing with SARs (Synthetic Aperture Radar) We process & visualize complex satellite data (SAR) into an interactive platform, turning raw telemetry into compelling visual insights and actionable stories about our changing planet.
summary:
### 🔥 FireWaltz – Earth Fire Intelligence

FireWaltz is an innovative wildfire monitoring and intelligence platform designed to help detect, track, analyze, and predict wildfire risks across the globe.

Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, FireWaltz aims to combine NASA Earth observation data, satellite imagery, and intelligent analysis to make wildfire information more accessible, understandable, and actionable.

### Key Features

* Interactive Global Map: Explore wildfire activity worldwide using an Earth visualization inspired by NASA's Blue Marble imagery.

* Wildfire Detection: Identify and monitor potential wildfire hotspots using satellite-based fire data.

* Ignis AI Assistant: An intelligent chatbot designed to answer questions about wildfires, fire detection, prevention, and environmental impacts.

* Wildfire Risk Analysis: Help users understand fire-prone regions and the environmental conditions that influence wildfire risks.

* Location-Based Exploration: Explore wildfire information across continents, countries, and specific locations.

* NASA Data Integration: Designed to incorporate NASA data sources for scientifically grounded wildfire insights.

### Our Mission

To transform complex satellite data into accessible wildfire intelligence, helping communities understand risks, improve preparedness, and protect lives, ecosystems, and the environment.

FireWaltz — Turning Satellite Data into Wildfire Intelligence.

Overview & Challenge Context

  • Project Name: FireWaltz — "The Hidden Dance of Wildfires: Seeing wildfire damage through smoke and clouds"
  • Event / Theme: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 · Dancing with the SARs
  • Team: Team FireWaltz

The Problem & Core Question

  • Problem: Wildfire landscape changes ("Before. After. Hidden.") are often obscured because smoke and clouds block the surface.
  • Core Question: "Can radar help us see what changed?"
